sources.outlet: NOTUS (now published as The Washington Sun; notus.org URL redirects here), co-published by Oklahoma Watch
sources.quote: A NOTUS analysis of a financial document Mullin filed Tuesday with the U.S. Senate revealed the Oklahoma lawmaker was months late disclosing nearly three dozen stock and bond transactions by himself and his wife.
sources.searcher_note: Second late filing (Aug 12, 2025): ~three dozen trades, $1.4M-$3.5M, mostly sales; says 'months late', not years. Mullin office: amended filing, third-party firm runs portfolio.

sources.outlet: NOTUS (now published as The Washington Sun; notus.org URL redirects here), co-published by Oklahoma Watch
sources.quote: The Oklahoma senator was two-and-a-half years late reporting seven stock purchases by his wife and about one-and-a-half years late disclosing three Oklahoma-connected municipal security purchases for himself
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found. First late filing (July 30, 2025): 10 trades, 2023 purchases, up to 2.5 years late. Oklahoma Watch republished 2025-08-05.

sources.quote: On Aug. 13, Mullin reported the sale or purchase of more than 70 stocks and bonds worth tens of millions of dollars in 2023 and 2024.
sources.searcher_note: Says Mullin blew past more deadlines than any lawmaker since Dec. 31, 2024; three late reports (Dec 31, July 30, Aug 13); July 30 filing was ten 2023 trades worth up to $735,000. Count (70+) differs from the lead's 48.

sources.quote: Others include Sens. Katie Britt (R-Alabama), Susan Collins (R-Maine), John Hickenlooper (D-Colorado), Mike Rounds (R-South Dakota), John Fetterman (D-Pennsylvania) and Mullin, whom Armstrong replaced.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff. Main subject is Armstrong (700 trades months late, $3.24M-$16.05M, third-party advisor direct indexing); lists Mullin among past-year STOCK Act violators.

sources.quote: One of the Senate’s newest members was months late disclosing 700 personal stock trades that together are worth millions of dollars, according to a NOTUS review of new congressional financial records.
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff copy of the NOTUS Armstrong story (same story as the Oklahoma Watch row); recorded for the Armstrong quote. Page also quotes the filing note: trades 'initiated by a third party advisor to implement a direct indexing strategy.'

notes: Mullin's late 2023-24 trade filings in summer 2025 were widely covered (NOTUS/Oklahoma Watch July 31 and Aug 13 2025, Benzinga Aug 1 2025 via Webull, Center Square Oct 7 2025, OU Daily, News9, OK Gazette). Press counts: 10 trades in the July 30 filing plus ~three dozen in the Aug 12 filing (NOTUS), or 70+ in the Aug 13 report (Center Square); NOTUS calls the second batch 'months late'. No source found stating 48 lines, 46 over a year late, 244-953 days, or a $1.74M floor. Newsweek (2026-03-16) on Mullin's DHS-era portfolio has no late-filing claims; NOTUS 2026-03-18 recaps the 2025 violations in one line. Mullin's office did not dispute lateness; it said filings were amended and a third-party firm runs the portfolio.
